caveats: NASADEM tiles were retrieved from the Microsoft Planetary Computer mirror of NASA LP DAAC NASADEM_HGT v001, not via an Earthdata login.
NASADEM void-fill quality layer was not available in the mirror; void-filled cells could not be masked.
Effective-resolution matching is a conservative identical Gaussian (σ = 30 m) on both planets; spectra are descriptive only.
Site percentiles use the median window; ranks are relative to the declared Earth null windows, not probabilities.
The Puna reference polygon location is low-confidence (pre-registered as such).
Terrain geometry does not establish geologic process, lithology, age or habitability.

breakdown.title: The Mars yardangs here are near the analysis limit
breakdown.text: Post-hoc diagnostic: the CTX yardang ridges repeat every ~246–481 m across-wind. At the pre-registered 180 m slope baseline and 30 m smoothing, a 250 m ridge keeps only ~26% of its gradient (~93% for km-scale ridges such as the Lut Kaluts). This plausibly explains why the fingerprint under-represents MFF elongation and failed validation; it does not change the result.

breakdown.title: Same shape at ≥180 m — not the same rock
breakdown.text: This tool measures terrain geometry only. Medusae Fossae material is debated (volcanic ash/ignimbrite or other fine, weakly cemented deposits) and is likely more porous and weaker than the Earth sites; lithology and induration are not measured here.
breakdown.source: de Silva et al. 2010, PSS 58:459 (ignimbrite yardangs as MFF analogs); lithology comparison needs verification per site

breakdown.title: Different air and gravity
breakdown.text: Mars has a surface pressure of roughly 0.6 kPa (≈1% of Earth's) and gravity of 3.71 m/s² (0.38 g). Wind erosion thresholds, abrasion rates and slope stability therefore differ; Earth gravity is identical at every Earth candidate.

breakdown.title: Different age and history
breakdown.text: Medusae Fossae deposits are generally considered Hesperian–Amazonian (billions of years); Earth yardang fields are far younger. Ages are not measured by this tool.

breakdown.title: Earth-only processes
breakdown.text: Rain, flowing water, frost and vegetation shape Earth deserts; NASADEM is a surface model, so any vegetation or buildings are included in heights.

breakdown.title: Different instruments
breakdown.text: Mars heights come from CTX stereo photogrammetry; Earth heights from the SRTM radar mission reprocessed as NASADEM. Both were resampled to the same 30 m grid and smoothed identically, but their error structures differ.
breakdown.source: USGS CTX DTM documentation; NASADEM user guide

breakdown.title: Fine detail is invisible at 30 m
breakdown.text: On the HiRISE crop, 13.9% of the area is steeper than 15° at a ~4 m baseline, but only 1.6% at the 180 m baseline used in the Earth comparison.

breakdown.title: Rover-scale questions are not evaluable on Earth here
breakdown.text: Only ~30 m public elevation exists for the Gobi candidates. Rover-relevant slopes, rocks and soil need drone or lidar survey; this tool does not estimate trafficability.
breakdown.source: Golombek et al. 2012, Space Sci Rev 170:641 (slope criteria at 2–5 m baselines)
